acceptance_checks: A task PR whose head task lowers risk_level from critical to low is blocked, and the Guardian requirement still resolves True.
A task PR that widens its own locks is blocked.
Changing scope, non_goals, required_skills, acceptance_checks or test_command alone is blocked — one case per field.
Changing status, expected_pr, closeout_pr, expected_branch or ledger_evidence alone is NOT blocked — one case per field.
A task file absent from the base snapshot (first registration) is NOT blocked.
A task file identical to base is NOT blocked.
A changed task file with no base snapshot available is blocked (fail closed).
The mutable-field set is the single constant already used by the ADR 0017 closeout classifier, not a second copy.
contract, goal_reconcile, post_merge_reconcile and bookkeeping-closeout PRs behave exactly as before, with no duplicated blocking reason.
tests/test_contract_immutability.py drives the gate for every case above.
scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh and scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh assert that the Guardian requirement survives a self-lowered risk_level, not merely that the PR blocks.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.
non_goals: Blocking status, expected_pr, closeout_pr, expected_branch or ledger_evidence
Changing contract, goal_reconcile, post_merge_reconcile or bookkeeping-closeout handling
Requiring a base snapshot for a first-registration PR
Changing risk resolution beyond refusing a weaker-than-base value
Touching any file outside the declared locks

scope:
In `scripts/mergegate_check.py`, enforce ADR 0015's Contract immutability on the NORMAL task-PR path: when a PR changes its own `.shiki/tasks/<task_id>.json`, compare the head task against the base snapshot and block when any governance field differs. The governance set is `scope`, `non_goals`, `required_skills`, `risk_level`, `locks`, `acceptance_checks`, `test_command`. Only `status`, `expected_pr`, `closeout_pr`, `expected_branch` and `ledger_evidence` may differ (the same mutable set the bookkeeping-closeout classifier already uses; reuse that constant rather than declaring a second list, so the two cannot drift).

Resolution is base-when-present, exactly as ADR 0015 states. When the task file exists in the base snapshot, the base is authority. When it does not — a first-registration PR, which is how the goal loop works today — head is authority and the PR passes. Additionally, `risk_level` may never resolve WEAKER than base: even where a field-equality rule might be relaxed later, a head value whose risk ordering is below the base value is always blocked. Fail closed when the base snapshot is missing but the comparison is required: a PR that changes its own task file with no base to check it against does not get a pass. A PR that does not touch its own task file is unaffected.

Do not disturb the modes that already have immutability rules: contract and goal_reconcile go through `_enforce_frozen_registration`, and post_merge_reconcile and the ADR 0017 closeout classifier have their own base comparisons. This rule applies to the normal path only, and must not double-report on those modes.

Add `tests/test_contract_immutability.py` covering, driven through the gate rather than by reading the source: risk_level lowered critical→low is blocked AND still yields guardian_required=True; locks widened is blocked; each of the other five governance fields changed is blocked, one case per field; every mutable field changed alone passes; a task file absent at base passes; a task file unchanged passes; a missing base snapshot with a changed task file is blocked. Add adversarial cases to `scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh` and `scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh` asserting specifically that the Guardian requirement survives a self-lowered risk_level — assert the guardian outcome, not merely that the PR blocks, so a future change that blocks for an unrelated reason cannot mask a regression.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: an implementation PR edits one field in its own task file and its Guardian gate disappears. Measured by driving the gate directly with a task whose base risk_level is `critical` and whose head risk_level is `low`: `enforce_untrusted_shiki_mutations` returned ZERO blocking reasons and `_builtin_guardian_risk_required` returned False. With head and base both `critical` the same call returns True. Nothing in the normal path objects to the change itself.
  Root cause: ADR 0015's Contract immutability was implemented only for the modes that register or reconcile contracts. `_frozen_task_match_errors` is reached from `_enforce_frozen_registration` (contract, goal_reconcile) only; `post_merge_reconcile` and the ADR 0017 closeout classifier have their own base comparisons; the normal task-PR path has none. `enforce_untrusted_shiki_mutations` blocks deleting a task file and blocks FOREIGN task files (`elif path != task_file`), but the PR's own task file is exempt, and `tasks` is absent from `_GENERIC_MIRROR_DIRS`.
  Exact change that reproduces this result: in the normal-path branch, load the base snapshot's task file and block when any of the seven governance fields differs, with base-when-present resolution and a never-weaker rule on risk_level.
  Why it matters more than it looks: every governance gain made on 2026-07-29/31 — contract approval before dispatch, the bookkeeping-closeout exemption, the drop from ~3.5 to ~0.3 operator approvals per task — is enforced downstream of a risk level the PR itself can rewrite.
  Reproducible when: a PR that lowers its own risk_level is blocked and still requires a Guardian, and a first-registration PR still passes.
test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && bash scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .
title: Bind a task PR's own contract to the base snapshot on the normal path
